result:
I found 12 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings, and fixed all of them. After the fixes, all 150 rules give the same results as the docstrings.

| Rule | What it did | Fixed to (per the docstring) |
|---|---|---|
| 02, 15, 38, 89, 149 | Rounded the discount with `round()` | Rounds down to the won with `// 100`, per the module docstring |
| 32 | Discount applied only above 5 units (`qty > 5`), so exactly 5 got nothing | Applies from 5 units (`qty >= 5`) |
| 74 | Discount started at 31 units | Starts at 30 units |
| 60 | Capped the price at 30,000 won, then took 10% of that | Takes 10% of the full price, then caps the discount at 30,000 won |
| 119 | 16% off | 15% off |
| 121 | Cap applied only when the discount was over 60,000 won, so discounts between 30,000 and 60,000 went uncapped | Always capped at 30,000 won |
| 126 | 11% off | 10% off |
| 140 | Counted only the units above the threshold (a "marginal" rule) | Discounts every unit (a "whole" rule), as the docstring says |

**How I checked:** I wrote a script that reads each rule's type, discount rate, threshold and cap from its docstring, then calculates the answer using the formulas in the module docstring. It compared each rule against that result for quantities 0–259, 500, 1,000 and 5,000, across 13 unit prices. Before the fixes it flagged exactly these 12 rules; after, none. The script and a backup of the original file are in the scratchpad, outside the project.

STATUS: DONE
